facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a cautious reading is the size and tenor of contracted revenue: remaining performance obligations on long-term customer arrangements were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30, terminal customers carry most operating costs, management says contracts are regularly amended and extended, and the filings report no write-downs of lease or time charter receivables in the nine months of 2026 or 2025. The controlling holder has also supported obligations, giving an uncapped construction and operating guarantee for a deepwater port and a letter of credit for its decommissioning, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or creditor exchange appears in the filings. The view would improve if executed debt documents showed tight limits on distributions and asset transfers, a contract schedule showed most terminal charters running well beyond the 2029 revolver maturity, and the Iraq and Colombia terminals started on the revised dates. It would worsen if a state customer delayed payment, force majeure turned into termination, or leverage moved toward the 3.25x level at which general distributions stop being permitted. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The defining transaction is the purchase of New Fortress Energy's Jamaica business, which closed on 2025-05-14. The initial cash price of USD 1,055.2 million fell by about USD 28.7 million after adjustments for cash, debt, expenses, working capital and inventory to USD 1,026.5 million, buying the Montego Bay and Old Harbour LNG terminals and the Clarendon power plant. The company recorded goodwill of about USD 235.0 million and customer-relationship intangibles of USD 369.0 million, and the business contributed USD 262.5 million of revenue and USD 53.9 million of net income from the closing date to year-end 2025. The company printed pro forma 2025 revenue of USD 1,376.5 million and net income of USD 201.7 million, as if the purchase and its funding had occurred on 2024-01-01. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation C05

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The new debt was one issue: the operating partnership's USD 800 million of senior unsecured notes due May 2030, issued at par under an indenture dated 2025-05-05 and guaranteed by certain direct and indirect restricted subsidiaries. Interest is paid each May and November. The proceeds, with USD 201.8 million of net equity proceeds from 8,000,000 new Class A shares and cash on hand, paid for the acquisition, repaid the term loan in full and covered fees. Alongside it the revolver was amended three times in 2025: the Fourth Amendment on 2025-03-26 added acquisition and debt baskets and a broader collateral maintenance covenant, the Fifth on 2025-04-21 extended maturity to March 2029 and raised commitments to USD 500.0 million, and the Sixth on 2025-09-26 gave more flexibility for investments and restricted payments. A Seventh Amendment dated 2025-12-31 is listed as an exhibit to the annual report but not described. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–105; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 155–157; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

facts.text: The Sponsor / Governance Risk Level is Medium. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is that the cash weakness reflects growth timing: operating cash flow exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million over nine months and by USD 312.40 million over twelve months, most capital spending is growth, many older contracts have been extended, the issuer states covenant compliance and none of the debt matures before 2029 apart from scheduled amortisation. If the Iraq, Colombia and conversion projects deliver contracted earnings on time, leverage should fall from 1.53x without new borrowing. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that protections cannot be verified: covenant levels are dated, an amendment is undescribed, customers are concentrated and sovereign-linked, and the carrier and conversion costs are unknown. The view would improve with executed documents showing wide headroom against a 3.25x distribution gate and the revolver tests, a contract schedule with long remaining terms, and on-time starts for Iraq and Colombia. It would worsen if the Iraq start slipped again, a state customer paid late, force majeure became termination, or free cash flow stayed negative after growth spending eased. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C01; calculation C02

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths, ranked. First, long-term take-or-pay terminal and supply contracts: remaining performance obligations of USD 18,329.6 million and a 5.8-year weighted average remaining terminal term give visible cash flow, which supports debt service and refinancing confidence. Second, moderate leverage with an equity cushion: 2.28x total and 1.53x net against earnings, with new equity funding part of the Jamaica purchase, which limits the leverage increase. Third, adequate liquidity: USD 856.74 million of cash and undrawn revolver with no maturity before 2029 beyond scheduled amortisation, which gives time to execute the growth plan. Fourth, a redeployable fleet of 12 floating regasification terminals, one onshore terminal and two LNG carriers at 2026-09-30, which lets a terminal move to a new contract, as Excelerate Acadia did to Jordan, and supports recovery value. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F06

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses, ranked. First, negative free cash flow in 2026 from growth spending, which drains cash and makes liquidity depend on the revolver. Second, concentrated, state-linked customers: four took 50% of revenue, so one payment failure would hit income and the revolver's tests. Third, deployment and supply risk from the Gulf conflict: the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027, which delays new earnings while capital is already committed. Fourth, structural subordination and weak protections: unsecured notes behind secured debt, control by one holder and an undescribed seventh amendment. Fifth, a 2030 maturity concentration of 74.24% of principal, which makes refinancing market-dependent in one year. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation F04; calculation F07

facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Excelerate owns and operates floating regasification terminals, an onshore terminal, LNG carriers and a combined heat and power plant, and sells LNG, gas and power. Its history of acquisition is short: a public listing in 2022, the purchase of the Sequoia terminal in 2023 and the Jamaica business in 2025. Visibility comes from fixed-rate take-or-pay charters under which customers generally bear fuel, port fees and boil-off, which supports debt service, but contracts can end on breach, change in law or extended force majeure, so visibility is conditional. Concentration is high and cyclicality sits in the LNG, gas and power line, which was 54.30% of nine-month revenue. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation F06

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: The registrant is a holding company with a controlling interest in the operating partnership, which borrows and issues the notes; 72.5% of the votes and of the partnership interests sit with a holder controlled by Kaiser. This is a controlled company relying on exemptions, with pro rata distributions, tax receivable agreement payments and a related-party sale-leaseback financing. Financial policy is moderate on evidence: payouts of USD 76.40 million in nine months (buybacks, dividends and distributions) sit within revolver restricted-payment limits of leverage at most 3.25x with liquidity of at least USD 200.0 million, or up to 3.0% of equity value a year, although the capacity used is not shown, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or creditor exchange appears in the filings; the Sponsor and governance risk level from the earlier analysis is Medium. The creditor risk is leakage capacity, not demonstrated leakage, and the notes are guaranteed only by certain restricted subsidiaries. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation F08; calculation C06

facts.text: Revenue is recurring in terminals and cyclical and concentrated in gas supply. Terminal charters are fixed-rate with escalators, customers generally bear fuel and port costs, many older contracts have already been extended and all owned floating terminals were contracted at 2025-12-31, so terminal income is predictable but terminable on stated events. LNG, gas and power revenue follows commodity prices and a few customers, and Qatar supply is under force majeure. Credit linkage: contracted income supports debt service as long as counterparties pay, while pass-through revenue inflates the denominator of any revenue-based ratio. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

facts.label: Margin resilience
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 129.3 million to USD 133.5 million between the third quarters (about 3.21%) even though LNG, gas and power revenue fell on fewer short-term sales and the timing of deliveries under the Atlantic Basin agreement, which cost USD 11.0 million, because the Jordan charter (USD 13.9 million) and short-term LNG opportunities (USD 6.1 million) more than offset it. Terminal margins are shielded from fuel and port costs that customers generally bear; LNG margins depend on back-to-back pricing that the issuer describes but the filings do not quantify. Business development costs rose by USD 3.4 million, so margins can be defended against volume timing but not shown to be defended against a protracted supply interruption. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C07

facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate: the issuer competes with other floating terminal owners, LNG sellers and LNG-to-power developers, and awards turn on experience, delivery speed and price. Entry is possible: the annual report notes limited availability of floating terminals in recent years but expects state-sponsored entities and major energy companies may buy, build or convert terminals, which would pressure rates on new and renewed contracts. The filings do not rank substitutes; the issuer's own example is gas displacing coal in Pakistan and Bangladesh. Buyer power is high because customers are few and state-linked, offset by take-or-pay terms and early-termination fees. Supplier power is high for LNG supply, as the Qatar force majeure shows, and for shipyard capacity, which drives the delivery dates of new terminals. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

facts.label: PEST factors
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are a primary driver here: the Middle East conflict, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and sovereign counterparties directly changed the Iraq timetable, Qatar supply and the Colombia plan. Economic factors matter through LNG prices (the Dutch gas benchmark averaged USD 17.62 per MMBtu and the Japan-Korea benchmark USD 19.77 in the third quarter, up from USD 15.61 and USD 17.65 in the second) and foreign currency fluctuations, which the annual report names as a risk. Social and technological factors are secondary; the planned reliquefaction unit on one terminal is an operating improvement, not a credit driver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C12

facts.label: SWOT
facts.text: Strengths are the contracts, a redeployable fleet and a record of extensions; weaknesses are customer concentration, negative free cash flow and structural subordination. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the Iraq, Colombia and Bahamas contracts and the conversion project, which add contracted earnings from 2027 and 2028, while the Sequoia extension through 2038 lengthens an existing contract. Threats are prolonged conflict, force majeure turning into termination, counterparty payment delay and any loosening of creditor protections through further amendments. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over twelve to twenty-four months tailwinds are the Colombia charter and Bahamas deliveries from the first quarter of 2027 and the Iraq start in the second quarter of 2027; headwinds are the Gulf conflict, the Qatar force majeure, the end of the nine-month Jordan charter that began in July 2026 unless it is extended, the carrier remainder due in the first quarter of 2027 and the conversion spending. Global LNG trade held up at about 101 million tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 against 106 in the third quarter of 2025, so import demand is resilient but supply is tight. Over three to five years the credit events are the 2029 revolver maturity and the May 2030 notes. Sector headwinds are price volatility and state counterparties; company headwinds are covenant uncertainty and control. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: An issuer-specific downside begins with the Gulf conflict continuing past the revised dates: the Iraq terminal slips again and Qatar supply stays under force majeure, interrupting LNG sales to Bangladesh. First break: LNG, gas and power margins and operating cash flow fall while committed growth spending on the carrier and conversion continues. Financial transmission: free cash flow stays negative, cash declines and the company draws the revolver, which lifts net leverage from 1.53x. Refinancing: the notes mature in May 2030 and a weaker leverage position raises refinancing cost, while distributions are gated at 3.25x leverage. Management levers are deferring growth spending, suspending buybacks and distributions and extending contracts; resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the next twelve months because maintenance spending is small, but not shown beyond that. Observable triggers are quarterly operating cash flow, revolver drawings and customer payment timing; no numerical stress is established. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Excelerate presents an adequate business profile supported by long-term take-or-pay charters, a redeployable fleet and moderate leverage, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow in 2026, concentrated state-linked customers, structural subordination of the unsecured notes and control by one holder. Cash-flow durability appears adequate before growth spending and weak after it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market conditions in 2030, when most principal falls due, and on whether the Iraq and Colombia contracts start on time. The primary downside path is continued Gulf disruption delaying contracted earnings while growth spending drains cash. Further analysis would require executed debt documents, covenant compliance figures, contract expiries and the cost of the carrier and conversion. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: deployment delay and negative free cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings support the requested financial, business and fundamental credit work with stated limits, but not covenant headroom, ratings or market-pricing views, because no credit agreement, indenture, rating report or quote was supplied. Creditors should treat leverage, liquidity and coverage as filing-based and headroom against the loan tests as unevidenced.

The latest evidence is the quarterly report for the period ended 2026-09-30, signed 2026-11-05, which leaves 13 days to the 2026-11-18 cutoff uncovered. Covenant levels are printed only in the annual reports, the latest as of year-end 2025, and the issuer's own ratio figures are printed nowhere. The May 2025 Jamaica acquisition makes 2025 comparatives only partly like-for-like.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Excelerate's leverage is moderate but has risen since the 2025 Jamaica acquisition, with net debt at 1.53x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 after net cash at the end of FY2024, so creditors depend on contracted terminal income to carry USD 1,075.91 million of debt.

Cash is the pressure point: free cash flow was negative USD 59.10 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 as growth spending outran operating cash flow, cash fell to USD 356.74 million, and the undrawn USD 500 million revolver is now the main buffer. Cash interest paid is still covered 4.45x by derived EBITDA. Covenant ratios are not printed, so headroom is not established.

### Financial interpretation

The balance sheet moved from net cash at the end of FY2024 to net debt after the 2025 financing: the senior unsecured 2030 notes and new equity funded the Jamaica acquisition and replaced the term loan, lifting carrying debt from 504.448 to 1098.261 (US$m) between the two year-ends. Net debt has since grown to 719.167 at 2026-09-30 while carrying debt eased to 1075.909, because cash fell by 181.492 as capital spending, buybacks and distributions outran operating cash flow. On derived last-twelve-months EBITDA of 470.901, total leverage is 2.28x and net leverage 1.53x; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of 488.193 they are 2.20x and 1.47x. Neither figure is a covenant calculation.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C07

That supports debt service as long as counterparties pay and terminals stay deployed; the figure uses commodity futures prices and includes LNG sales, so it overstates terminal income. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 5.02x for FY2025 and 4.45x on the last twelve months; FY2025 cash interest holds only part of a year of the 2030 notes, so the burden will be higher on a full-year basis.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C06; calculation C07

Cash flow quality weakened in 2026. Operating cash flow was 254.502 for the nine months against 356.821 a year earlier, which the issuer attributes to the timing of collections and payments on LNG purchases and sales and to interest on the 2030 notes. Purchases of property and equipment were 313.606, including the final milestone of about 210 on the new floating terminal, so levered free cash flow was negative 59.104. The last-twelve-months figure is positive at 11.672 only because FY2025 was strong. Buybacks of 38.146 and dividends and distributions of 38.250 were paid on top, so the shortfall was funded from cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C12; calculation C13

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is unrestricted cash of 356.742 plus an undrawn revolver of 500.0, or 856.742, with no letters of credit issued under the revolver and a March 2029 maturity. The issuer separately has letters of credit of 172.8 outstanding under a bilateral facility whose size and expiry are not stated. Contractual obligations for the next twelve months are 1014.369, of which LNG purchase and capacity obligations are 750.307 and long-term debt obligations 35.957; the issuer says the LNG it sources is primarily sold on a back-to-back price basis, which offsets part of that call on cash. A dividend and distribution of 10.301 is payable on 2026-12-03.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C08; calculation C11

Deferred revenue is a modest non-debt funding source that is running down: total deferred revenue fell from 86.331 at the start of 2026 to 65.229 at 2026-09-30, and the current portion alone consumed 19.837 of operating cash in the nine months. A further slowdown in customer advances would remove operating funding before revenue declines, so it should be read with the weaker operating cash flow.

Data-quality and definition risks are bounded. The statements foot in every column, nine-month figures reconcile to the quarterly reports, and the FY2024 comparatives agree with the FY2024 annual report. The main risks are that reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer prints only an adjusted figure, that 2025 comparatives hold Jamaica for part of the year, that the nine-month 2025 and FY2025 acquisition cash differ by 28.661 without explanation, and that covenant levels are printed only as of year-end 2025 with no reported ratio.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C03; calculation C14

Claims outside Total Debt are sizeable and none is in the leverage figures. Finance lease liabilities of 152.329 and operating lease liabilities of 146.924 (25.881 current plus 121.043 long-term) sit on their own balance-sheet lines, and the tax receivable agreement liability is 57.651 (7.685 current plus 49.966 long-term), owed to the Kaiser-controlled holder of the Class B interests at 85% of realised tax savings. LNG purchase and capacity obligations are 750.307 within twelve months and 11520.239 beyond, other purchase obligations 159.977 within twelve months, and asset retirement obligations 65.343. The filings print no defined-benefit pension, retiree medical, factoring or supplier-finance arrangement; the only retirement plan is a defined contribution plan. Adding the finance leases to Total Debt would give 1228.238 at 2026-09-30.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; calculation C17; calculation C18

Covenants are printed only as of year-end 2025 and no issuer-reported ratio or headroom is given for any date. The revolver requires a maximum consolidated total leverage of 3.50x, rising to 4.25x when aggregate unsecured debt is USD 250.0 million or more (on the filing's wording the higher level applies while the unsecured 2030 notes are outstanding), a minimum consolidated interest coverage of 2.50x, and collateral coverage of at least the greater of USD 750.0 million and 130% of credit exposure; the March 2025 amendment broadened the collateral test. The Experience financing requires minimum equity of 500.0, a maximum debt-to-equity ratio of 3.5 to 1 and minimum cash and availability of 20.0, and the Bangladesh loans a quarterly project debt service cover of at least 1.10. The issuer states compliance with all covenants at 2026-09-30. The covenant definitions differ from the metrics computed here, so no headroom is calculated.

The nine months brought no new borrowing and show repayments of long-term debt of 17.323 and related-party debt of 7.792, share repurchases of 10.4 in the third quarter (291,157 shares at a weighted average price of 35.21 dollars), and a dividend of 0.09 dollars per Class A share declared on 2026-10-29. The Jamaica arbitration concluded in September 2026 with an award of 36.340 inclusive of interest and fees, retained by the seller and secured by escrow, and paid in October 2026. In March 2026 a force majeure notice was received from QatarEnergy and passed on under the supply agreement with Petrobangla. The new terminal, Excelerate Acadia, was delivered in the second quarter of 2026 for a final milestone payment of about 210, and began a nine-month charter in Jordan in July 2026. Contracts were signed in 2026 for Colombia (seven years from the first quarter of 2027), a five-year Sequoia extension through 2038 and the Bahamas hub, and the Seatrium conversion contract was awarded in October 2026 with no value stated.

A downside sequence the filings support begins with a force majeure or shipping disruption that interrupts purchased LNG supply, which the issuer already faces on its Qatar purchase agreement and passes on to Petrobangla under its long-term supply agreement. A first break would show in LNG, gas and power margins and operating cash flow, followed by lower EBITDA and thinner cash against the rising capital programme and shareholder payments; the observable tests are quarterly operating cash flow, the revolver availability and the year-end covenant disclosure. No numerical stress is established here.

## Gaps

- Unadjusted EBITDA is not printed for any period; the issuer reports only Adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from printed components and every leverage and cover ratio rests on that derivation. The restriction is on comparison with any lender definition. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the covenant definition of consolidated EBITDA.

- Covenant ratios and headroom are not printed in any period, and the covenant levels are printed only in the annual reports as of year-end 2025, so headroom against the leverage, interest cover and collateral tests cannot be calculated. Severity: High. Action: obtain the latest compliance certificate and the credit agreement definitions.

- The year-by-year debt maturity ladder is printed only at 2025-12-31; the third-quarter report prints twelve-month and beyond totals, so the ladder is not rolled forward to 2026-09-30. Severity: Medium. Action: use the dated ladder or obtain the amortisation schedules.

- Instrument carrying values for the 2030 notes and the other financings are not disclosed separately, only one aggregate issuance-cost adjustment, so instrument-level carrying values are not stated. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for leverage, which uses balance-sheet totals.

- The size, expiry and collateral of the bilateral letter of credit facility, under which 172.8 of letters of credit are outstanding at 2026-09-30, are not stated, so remaining capacity is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the facility terms.

- The legal rank of the Experience, Exquisite and Bangladesh terminal financings against the revolver and the 2030 notes is not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and the stack is partial. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the security and intercreditor documents.

- The company reports one segment, so no segment schedule is stated and no segment revenue or earnings sum is given; revenue is split only between terminal services and LNG, gas and power. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Interest income is not printed separately from other income, net, so interest income is not stated for any period. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the derived EBITDA, which keeps other income inside it.

- The cash-flow statements for the interim periods print no line for gain or loss on non-cash items or for the tax receivable agreement liability, so those two lines are not supplied for the nine-month columns. Severity: Low. Action: none; the operating cash flow totals foot without them.

- Source dashes are kept as missing rather than zero for the lines of the cash flow statements and balance sheets that print them: acquisition cash, Class A issuance, Class A repurchases, debt issuance, debt issuance costs, the gain or loss on non-cash items, and goodwill, intangible assets and deferred tax liability at 2024-12-31. Totals foot without them. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for leverage or cover.

- The nine-month 2025 acquisition cash of 1048.091 and the FY2025 figure of 1019.430 differ by 28.661 with no explanation in the filings. Severity: Low. Action: confirm the post-closing adjustment with the issuer.

- The purchase price of the LNG carrier and the value of the conversion contract are not stated, so their effect on net debt after 2026-09-30 is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the amounts from management.

- Nothing after the third-quarter report's signature date is covered, and the purchase of the carrier, the conversion contract and the dividend payment are future or partly future cash events at the cutoff. Severity: Low. Action: refresh with any later filing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Excelerate is a contracted LNG-terminal and gas-supply business whose credit strength rests on long-term take-or-pay income from a mix of state-owned, utility and industrial customers, so creditors should weigh counterparty, concentration and deployment risk, and the control held by one shareholder, above scale.

The contracted base is real but moving: the Iraq terminal start has slipped from the third quarter of 2026 to the second quarter of 2027, four customers took 50% of nine-month revenue, and one holder controls 72.5% of the voting power. Contract expiries, executed debt documents and board composition are not supplied, so legal protection and renewal risk are not established.
### Key findings

- Contracted terminal income is the credit anchor but not the majority of revenue: terminal services were 45.70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the rest was LNG, gas and power sales, which pass most commodity cost through and carry a thinner margin, since the cost of LNG, gas and power equalled 81.59% of those sales. Minimum contracted cash flows at the 2025 year-end were USD 3,315.2 million for terminal services with a weighted average remaining term of 5.8 years, and USD 17,031.2 million for LNG, gas and power with 9.3 years.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C01; calculation C09

- Counterparty and concentration risk is the main revenue risk, because four customers each took at least 10% and together 50% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and the largest alone took 16%. Customers include state-owned energy companies in emerging markets, so credit support depends on sovereign-linked payment performance; the filings report no write-down of trade receivables on lease or time charter services in the nine months of 2026 or 2025.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C03

- Control sits with one shareholder and the company is a controlled company relying on exemptions from independence requirements: a holding company controlled by Kaiser owns all Class B shares and 72.5% of the combined voting power, and also receives payments under a tax receivable agreement. Distributions to public and Class B holders are pro rata, but the revolver permits general distributions only while liquidity is at least USD 200.0 million and leverage is at most 3.25x, with separate baskets for tax, tax receivable agreement and overhead payments, and no sponsor extraction beyond pro rata payouts is documented.

- The 2025 Jamaica acquisition changed the risk profile: it cost USD 1,026.5 million after adjustments, was funded by USD 800 million of senior unsecured notes due 2030, USD 201.8 million of new equity and cash on hand, and added the Jamaica gas and power business, so North America including the Caribbean is now 41.30% of revenue by region. Equity covered a minority of the price, so the purchase raised debt, and the sources and uses of funds are not printed.

- Deployment is the live operating risk: the Gulf conflict moved the Iraq start from the third quarter of 2026 to the second quarter of 2027, forced a force majeure exchange with Qatari and Bangladeshi counterparties, redirected the new terminal to a nine-month Jordan charter, and changed the Colombia plan from redeploying one terminal to using other terminals outside the Gulf. Earnings now depend on redeploying assets on schedule, not only on contracts already signed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ee-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C06

- Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for legal protection: statements are audited and quarterly, yet the covenant terms are summarised only, contract expiry dates by terminal are not in the extracted text, and a seventh credit agreement amendment dated 2025-12-31 is listed as an exhibit without any description.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a cautious reading is the size and tenor of contracted revenue: remaining performance obligations on long-term customer arrangements were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30, terminal customers carry most operating costs, management says contracts are regularly amended and extended, and the filings report no write-downs of lease or time charter receivables in the nine months of 2026 or 2025. The controlling holder has also supported obligations, giving an uncapped construction and operating guarantee for a deepwater port and a letter of credit for its decommissioning, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or creditor exchange appears in the filings.

The view would improve if executed debt documents showed tight limits on distributions and asset transfers, a contract schedule showed most terminal charters running well beyond the 2029 revolver maturity, and the Iraq and Colombia terminals started on the revised dates. It would worsen if a state customer delayed payment, force majeure turned into termination, or leverage moved toward the 3.25x level at which general distributions stop being permitted.
### Limitations

- Contract expiry dates and day rates by terminal are not in the extracted text, so the conclusion that contracted income anchors credit cannot be dated and stays qualitative until a contract schedule is supplied.

- No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied and a seventh amendment is not described, so the restricted-payment gate of 3.25x and USD 200.0 million, taken from the 2025 annual report, may have changed and the control conclusion rests on a summary.

- Board composition, the stockholder's agreement terms and the income-statement related-party amounts are not in the extracted text, so the governance conclusion is limited to the controlled-company structure and cannot assess board independence or fees.
- Customers are anonymised as lettered customers, so the counterparty conclusion cannot rest on any named credit standing or country limit.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The defining transaction is the purchase of New Fortress Energy's Jamaica business, which closed on 2025-05-14. The initial cash price of USD 1,055.2 million fell by about USD 28.7 million after adjustments for cash, debt, expenses, working capital and inventory to USD 1,026.5 million, buying the Montego Bay and Old Harbour LNG terminals and the Clarendon power plant. The company recorded goodwill of about USD 235.0 million and customer-relationship intangibles of USD 369.0 million, and the business contributed USD 262.5 million of revenue and USD 53.9 million of net income from the closing date to year-end 2025. The company printed pro forma 2025 revenue of USD 1,376.5 million and net income of USD 201.7 million, as if the purchase and its funding had occurred on 2024-01-01.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation C05

The new debt was one issue: the operating partnership's USD 800 million of senior unsecured notes due May 2030, issued at par under an indenture dated 2025-05-05 and guaranteed by certain direct and indirect restricted subsidiaries. Interest is paid each May and November. The proceeds, with USD 201.8 million of net equity proceeds from 8,000,000 new Class A shares and cash on hand, paid for the acquisition, repaid the term loan in full and covered fees. Alongside it the revolver was amended three times in 2025: the Fourth Amendment on 2025-03-26 added acquisition and debt baskets and a broader collateral maintenance covenant, the Fifth on 2025-04-21 extended maturity to March 2029 and raised commitments to USD 500.0 million, and the Sixth on 2025-09-26 gave more flexibility for investments and restricted payments. A Seventh Amendment dated 2025-12-31 is listed as an exhibit to the annual report but not described.

No new debt was raised in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Instead the company signed growth commitments that will need funding: the acquisition of an LNG carrier in July 2026 for a first floating storage and regasification conversion, with a ten percent downpayment in the third quarter and the remainder due in the first quarter of 2027; a conversion contract awarded to Seatrium in October 2026; and a share repurchase program of up to USD 75.0 million approved in December 2025, under which USD 36.246 million of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30. Neither the carrier price nor the conversion contract value is stated, so the borrowing need for 2027 is not established.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Excelerate Energy, Inc. (issuer ee-1888447) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot (full credit assessment) pathway. Scope is the business profile, financial profile, outlook, downside, ranked drivers and monitoring triggers drawn from the supplied filings and the three earlier analyses. No rating, relative-value view or sizing is given.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 515190c356e4198e7910e91dc74c994c3c49d0608fdcaf86cf980e8867e897ce | Latest statements, debt, liquidity, contracted revenue, business updates, ownership and subsequent events. Date is the signature date. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 | 44f4467217019052423cca82114393555851a3f2490f7ab94f067cd1010d7570 | Contract terms, covenant levels, competition, control, related parties, maturities, capital spending split. Date is the signature date. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_ee-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-06 | 5ba230489f112e0a4054c4e55766dcb0449aa15bea18c0bc0bdd1c2ef96651a5 | Iraq timetable and Colombia plan as reported in the second quarter. Date is the signature date. |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_ee-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-27 | 092c7b5959d8fdd2870ce56d8b907dd50e478b94c19ee8f8dab24cbf5447d68c | Not relied on for any figure here; inventory only, used by earlier analyses for FY2024 comparatives. Date is the signature date. |
| Supplied analysis | Module | sha256 | Use |

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Excelerate's credit is adequate: contracted take-or-pay income and moderate leverage support debt service, but negative 2026 free cash flow, concentrated state-linked customers and delayed deployments leave creditors reliant on the undrawn revolver and unproven covenant headroom.

Net debt was 1.53x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 1.55x pro forma for the dividend and distribution payable on 2026-12-03, and EBITDA covered cash interest 4.45x. Free cash flow was negative USD 59.10 million in the nine months, but operating cash flow still exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million, so the weakness is growth spending, not core earnings, and the next growth costs are not stated.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F01; calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation C01
### Key findings

- The business profile is adequate, anchored on contracts rather than scale: terminal services were 45.70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and remaining performance obligations were USD 18,329.6 million at 2026-09-30. At the 2025 year-end terminal charters held minimum contracted cash flows of USD 3,315.2 million over a weighted average 5.8 years, against USD 17,031.2 million for LNG, gas and power contracts, which are 83.71% of the combined USD 20,346.4 million. Most long-dated contract value is therefore gas supply with commodity pass-through and counterparty exposure, so headline visibility overstates the protected terminal income.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation F06; calculation C10

- Leverage is moderate and has risen from net cash: total debt was 2.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA and net debt 1.53x at 2026-09-30, or 1.55x pro forma for the payment due 2026-12-03. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the figures are lower, so the choice of EBITDA does not change the conclusion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02

- Cash generation is the weak point, not earnings: nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 59.10 million because growth spending of about USD 286.69 million outran operating cash flow, which itself fell 28.68% on collection and payment timing in LNG sales and higher interest on the notes. Operating cash flow still exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million, and the final payment of about USD 210 million on the Excelerate Acadia terminal is complete, but the carrier balance and conversion contract that follow have no stated cost.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation F04; calculation C01; calculation C09; calculation C13

- Liquidity is adequate: cash plus the undrawn revolver was USD 856.74 million at 2026-09-30, before the dividend and distribution of USD 10.30 million payable on 2026-12-03 and the October 2026 events, with the revolver undrawn and maturing in March 2029. The refinancing risk is concentrated in time rather than near: 74.24% of principal at the 2025 year-end falls due in 2030, mostly the unsecured notes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F05; calculation C04

- Counterparty and deployment risks are the main earnings risks: four customers took 50% of nine-month revenue, partly because some buy large LNG and gas volumes, the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027 and a supply force majeure notice is outstanding. The new Iraq-related cash flows are therefore later than the annual report indicated.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation F07

- Structure and control weaken creditor protection: the unsecured notes of USD 800 million rank behind a USD 500 million secured revolver and USD 288.47 million of financings secured on specific assets (USD 788.47 million if the revolver were drawn in full), a holder controlling 72.5% of the votes receives tax receivable agreement payments, and a seventh credit agreement amendment is undescribed, so covenant headroom is not established even though the issuer states it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C05; calculation F08
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is that the cash weakness reflects growth timing: operating cash flow exceeded maintenance capital spending by USD 220.92 million over nine months and by USD 312.40 million over twelve months, most capital spending is growth, many older contracts have been extended, the issuer states covenant compliance and none of the debt matures before 2029 apart from scheduled amortisation. If the Iraq, Colombia and conversion projects deliver contracted earnings on time, leverage should fall from 1.53x without new borrowing.

The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that protections cannot be verified: covenant levels are dated, an amendment is undescribed, customers are concentrated and sovereign-linked, and the carrier and conversion costs are unknown. The view would improve with executed documents showing wide headroom against a 3.25x distribution gate and the revolver tests, a contract schedule with long remaining terms, and on-time starts for Iraq and Colombia. It would worsen if the Iraq start slipped again, a state customer paid late, force majeure became termination, or free cash flow stayed negative after growth spending eased.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C01; calculation C02
### Limitations

- Covenant levels come from the 2025 annual report and an undescribed seventh amendment may have changed them, so the view that leverage is moderate is relative to the market and not to covenant headroom, which stays not established.

- Contract expiries and customer names are not available, so the adequate revenue durability rests on weighted average terms; a cluster of near-term expiries would lower the profile and the liquidity view.
- The cost of the carrier purchase and the conversion contract is not stated, so the adequate liquidity assessment excludes a funding call that could be material in 2027 and would reduce it.
- No rating, market price or peer data was supplied, so the business profile is judged against the filings alone and its standing against comparable issuers is not established.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths, ranked. First, long-term take-or-pay terminal and supply contracts: remaining performance obligations of USD 18,329.6 million and a 5.8-year weighted average remaining terminal term give visible cash flow, which supports debt service and refinancing confidence. Second, moderate leverage with an equity cushion: 2.28x total and 1.53x net against earnings, with new equity funding part of the Jamaica purchase, which limits the leverage increase. Third, adequate liquidity: USD 856.74 million of cash and undrawn revolver with no maturity before 2029 beyond scheduled amortisation, which gives time to execute the growth plan. Fourth, a redeployable fleet of 12 floating regasification terminals, one onshore terminal and two LNG carriers at 2026-09-30, which lets a terminal move to a new contract, as Excelerate Acadia did to Jordan, and supports recovery value.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F06

Weaknesses, ranked. First, negative free cash flow in 2026 from growth spending, which drains cash and makes liquidity depend on the revolver. Second, concentrated, state-linked customers: four took 50% of revenue, so one payment failure would hit income and the revolver's tests. Third, deployment and supply risk from the Gulf conflict: the Iraq start moved to the second quarter of 2027, which delays new earnings while capital is already committed. Fourth, structural subordination and weak protections: unsecured notes behind secured debt, control by one holder and an undescribed seventh amendment. Fifth, a 2030 maturity concentration of 74.24% of principal, which makes refinancing market-dependent in one year.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation F04; calculation F07
### Company description and credit linkage

Excelerate owns and operates floating regasification terminals, an onshore terminal, LNG carriers and a combined heat and power plant, and sells LNG, gas and power. Its history of acquisition is short: a public listing in 2022, the purchase of the Sequoia terminal in 2023 and the Jamaica business in 2025. Visibility comes from fixed-rate take-or-pay charters under which customers generally bear fuel, port fees and boil-off, which supports debt service, but contracts can end on breach, change in law or extended force majeure, so visibility is conditional. Concentration is high and cyclicality sits in the LNG, gas and power line, which was 54.30% of nine-month revenue.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation F06
### Ownership and group structure

The registrant is a holding company with a controlling interest in the operating partnership, which borrows and issues the notes; 72.5% of the votes and of the partnership interests sit with a holder controlled by Kaiser. This is a controlled company relying on exemptions, with pro rata distributions, tax receivable agreement payments and a related-party sale-leaseback financing. Financial policy is moderate on evidence: payouts of USD 76.40 million in nine months (buybacks, dividends and distributions) sit within revolver restricted-payment limits of leverage at most 3.25x with liquidity of at least USD 200.0 million, or up to 3.0% of equity value a year, although the capacity used is not shown, and no dividend recapitalisation, priming or creditor exchange appears in the filings; the Sponsor and governance risk level from the earlier analysis is Medium. The creditor risk is leakage capacity, not demonstrated leakage, and the notes are guaranteed only by certain restricted subsidiaries.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation F08; calculation C06
### Revenue durability

Revenue is recurring in terminals and cyclical and concentrated in gas supply. Terminal charters are fixed-rate with escalators, customers generally bear fuel and port costs, many older contracts have already been extended and all owned floating terminals were contracted at 2025-12-31, so terminal income is predictable but terminable on stated events. LNG, gas and power revenue follows commodity prices and a few customers, and Qatar supply is under force majeure. Credit linkage: contracted income supports debt service as long as counterparties pay, while pass-through revenue inflates the denominator of any revenue-based ratio.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10
### Margin resilience

Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 129.3 million to USD 133.5 million between the third quarters (about 3.21%) even though LNG, gas and power revenue fell on fewer short-term sales and the timing of deliveries under the Atlantic Basin agreement, which cost USD 11.0 million, because the Jordan charter (USD 13.9 million) and short-term LNG opportunities (USD 6.1 million) more than offset it. Terminal margins are shielded from fuel and port costs that customers generally bear; LNG margins depend on back-to-back pricing that the issuer describes but the filings do not quantify. Business development costs rose by USD 3.4 million, so margins can be defended against volume timing but not shown to be defended against a protracted supply interruption.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C07
### Cash conversion and capital intensity

Last-twelve-months operating cash flow was almost the same as capital spending (1.03x), so free cash flow was thin, while maintenance spending was small: 33.585 of 320.278 gross in nine months (10.49%). Cash interest paid took 22.46% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, and the notes' annual coupon of USD 64.0 million is paid in May and November. Capex flexibility is real because most spending is growth and the largest 2026 outflow, the Acadia milestone, is complete, but projects with signed contracts (Iraq, Colombia, the carrier and conversion) are committed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C11
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is moderate: the issuer competes with other floating terminal owners, LNG sellers and LNG-to-power developers, and awards turn on experience, delivery speed and price. Entry is possible: the annual report notes limited availability of floating terminals in recent years but expects state-sponsored entities and major energy companies may buy, build or convert terminals, which would pressure rates on new and renewed contracts. The filings do not rank substitutes; the issuer's own example is gas displacing coal in Pakistan and Bangladesh. Buyer power is high because customers are few and state-linked, offset by take-or-pay terms and early-termination fees. Supplier power is high for LNG supply, as the Qatar force majeure shows, and for shipyard capacity, which drives the delivery dates of new terminals.
### PEST factors

Political and regulatory factors are a primary driver here: the Middle East conflict, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and sovereign counterparties directly changed the Iraq timetable, Qatar supply and the Colombia plan. Economic factors matter through LNG prices (the Dutch gas benchmark averaged USD 17.62 per MMBtu and the Japan-Korea benchmark USD 19.77 in the third quarter, up from USD 15.61 and USD 17.65 in the second) and foreign currency fluctuations, which the annual report names as a risk. Social and technological factors are secondary; the planned reliquefaction unit on one terminal is an operating improvement, not a credit driver.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C12
### SWOT

Strengths are the contracts, a redeployable fleet and a record of extensions; weaknesses are customer concentration, negative free cash flow and structural subordination. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the Iraq, Colombia and Bahamas contracts and the conversion project, which add contracted earnings from 2027 and 2028, while the Sequoia extension through 2038 lengthens an existing contract. Threats are prolonged conflict, force majeure turning into termination, counterparty payment delay and any loosening of creditor protections through further amendments.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37
### T2.7 Financial Profile Scorecard
| Dimension | Assessment | Credit Rationale |

| Scale / market position | Average | Controls or operates 12 floating regasification terminals, one onshore terminal and two LNG carriers, and states it is the largest provider of regasified LNG capacity in five countries; LTM EBITDA is USD 470.901 million; no peer data was supplied. |
| Competitive advantage | Average | Long contracts and a redeployable fleet help, but contracts are terminable on stated events and the leadership claim is Management Language. |
| Business diversification | Weak | Four customers took 50% of revenue and North America including the Caribbean is 41.30% of revenue; two business lines. |

| Cost and capex flexibility | Average | Customers generally bear fuel and port costs and uncommitted growth spending is deferrable, but signed projects and the carrier and conversion commitments are committed. |
| Margin stability | Average | Terminal income is fixed-rate; LNG margins depend on back-to-back pricing and timing of deliveries. |
| Free cash flow stability | Weak | Levered free cash flow was 298.225 in FY2025, 131.180 in FY2024 and negative 59.104 in nine months of 2026. |

| Ability to refinance / access capital markets | Average | USD 800 million of notes were placed in 2025 and the revolver matures in March 2029, but no rating or market price was supplied and 74.24% of principal falls due in 2030. |

| Liquidity position | Average | Cash plus undrawn revolver of 856.742 against twelve-month debt principal of 35.957, with covenant headroom and the bilateral letter of credit facility not established. |

| Financial policy and governance | Average | Moderate payouts within restricted-payment limits that a sixth amendment relaxed, and an equity-funded part of the acquisition, offset by control by one holder and an undescribed seventh amendment. |

Main supports are contracted income, moderate leverage and a long-dated debt profile; constraints are weak free cash flow, concentration and structure; the trend is leverage rising from net cash while cash falls; the key missing data are covenant headroom, contract expiries and the cost of the carrier and conversion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F01; calculation F05; calculation C04
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over twelve to twenty-four months tailwinds are the Colombia charter and Bahamas deliveries from the first quarter of 2027 and the Iraq start in the second quarter of 2027; headwinds are the Gulf conflict, the Qatar force majeure, the end of the nine-month Jordan charter that began in July 2026 unless it is extended, the carrier remainder due in the first quarter of 2027 and the conversion spending. Global LNG trade held up at about 101 million tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 against 106 in the third quarter of 2025, so import demand is resilient but supply is tight. Over three to five years the credit events are the 2029 revolver maturity and the May 2030 notes. Sector headwinds are price volatility and state counterparties; company headwinds are covenant uncertainty and control.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12
### Downside scenario

An issuer-specific downside begins with the Gulf conflict continuing past the revised dates: the Iraq terminal slips again and Qatar supply stays under force majeure, interrupting LNG sales to Bangladesh. First break: LNG, gas and power margins and operating cash flow fall while committed growth spending on the carrier and conversion continues. Financial transmission: free cash flow stays negative, cash declines and the company draws the revolver, which lifts net leverage from 1.53x. Refinancing: the notes mature in May 2030 and a weaker leverage position raises refinancing cost, while distributions are gated at 3.25x leverage. Management levers are deferring growth spending, suspending buybacks and distributions and extending contracts; resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the next twelve months because maintenance spending is small, but not shown beyond that. Observable triggers are quarterly operating cash flow, revolver drawings and customer payment timing; no numerical stress is established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ee-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_ee-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C01; calculation F01

### Overall credit view

Overall, Excelerate presents an adequate business profile supported by long-term take-or-pay charters, a redeployable fleet and moderate leverage, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow in 2026, concentrated state-linked customers, structural subordination of the unsecured notes and control by one holder. Cash-flow durability appears adequate before growth spending and weak after it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market conditions in 2030, when most principal falls due, and on whether the Iraq and Colombia contracts start on time. The primary downside path is continued Gulf disruption delaying contracted earnings while growth spending drains cash. Further analysis would require executed debt documents, covenant compliance figures, contract expiries and the cost of the carrier and conversion. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: deployment delay and negative free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
